title: Payment Arrangement Renegotiation of the Installment Count
content:
# Payment Arrangement Renegotiation of the Installment Count

## Clauses in force

1. An active Payment Arrangement plan may have its installment count changed only where the kind allows renegotiation (its renegotiations allowed is above zero) and the plan has not been renegotiated before.
2. Renegotiation is made only on a plan in active status with no installment currently counted as missed, as the plan record shows.
3. Renegotiation never changes the deferred amount or re-ages any missed installment.

A renegotiation records the new total installment count, counting the installments already billed, and the new regular installment for the installments not yet billed.

## Retired clauses

- The former clause that the new total installment count, counting installments already billed, may not exceed the kind's renegotiation ceiling, and that the regular installment for the installments not yet billed is the unbilled plan balance divided by the number of installments remaining, rounded down to the cent, with the final installment carrying the remainder, is **no longer in force**; it has been superseded by the current basis.
- The former clause that the new count is chosen by the customer is **no longer in force**; it has been superseded by the current basis.

## Points of judgement (hypothetical plans)

| Plan | Status | Installment counted as missed | Renegotiated before | Kind allows renegotiation | May be renegotiated |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Standard Deferred Payment Agreement | Active | None | No | Yes | Yes |
| Extended Deferred Payment Agreement | Active | One | No | Yes | No |
| Standard Deferred Payment Agreement | Active | None | Yes | Yes | No |
| Short-Term Installment Plan | Active | None | No | No | No |

superseded_clauses: The new total installment count, counting installments already billed, may not exceed renegotiation_max_total_installments, and the regular installment for the installments not yet billed is the unbilled plan balance divided by the number of installments remaining, rounded down to the cent, with the final installment carrying the remainder.
The new count is chosen by the customer.
